script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Good morning! I'm Dr. Martinez. What brings you and little Emma in today?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Hi, um, she's had a fever for two days now and she's just been so fussy. I'm really worried something's wrong.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: I can understand why you're concerned. Let's figure out what's going on. What's her temperature been running?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: It got up to 101.8 yesterday and this morning it was 101.2. I've been giving her Tylenol but I don't know if I'm doing it right.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's a good fever to keep track of. How much Tylenol have you been giving her and how often?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: The bottle said 1.25 milliliters every four hours, so that's what I've been doing. Is that okay?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's exactly right for her weight. Good job. Any other symptoms like vomiting, diarrhea, or changes in eating?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: She's been eating less, maybe half her normal bottles. And she seems more sleepy but also more cranky at the same time.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's pretty typical when babies don't feel well. Let me take a look at her now. I'm going to check her ears first.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Oh, she's starting to fuss again. She hates having her ears looked at.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: I can see she's not happy about this, but her ears actually look good. Now let me listen to her chest.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Really? Her ears are okay? I was sure it was an ear infection.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Her lungs sound clear too. I'm going to check her throat now - this might make her cry a bit more.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Okay, I've got her. Poor baby.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Her throat looks a little red but not severely inflamed. Based on everything I'm seeing, this looks like a viral infection.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: So no antibiotics? How long will this last? I just want her to feel better.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Viruses typically run their course in 5 to 7 days. Keep doing exactly what you're doing with the Tylenol. You're taking great care of her.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Thank you. When should I worry and bring her back?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: If her fever goes above 102.5 or she stops eating completely, call us right away. Otherwise, you're doing everything right.
